title: language factor is typescript but the deliverable is plain CommonJS JavaScript
evidence: stack.json language="typescript"; the only source files are server.js and test.js (CommonJS require/module.exports, server.js:1-3, server.js:201); package-lock.json has no node_modules/typescript entry and package.json declares no typescript/ts-jest/@types dependency; TASK.md 'Technical constraints' says 'Use the specified language and framework'. Sibling cells of the same task did emit .ts (e.g. ..._stack=q4/rep4/src/server.ts). The idiomatic scorer returned 0.0 in scores.json.
suggestion: Author server.ts/test.ts with a tsconfig.json and ts-jest (or compile with tsc), so the run actually exercises the typescript level of the language factor.

title: SUMMARY.md and FINAL_SUMMARY.md make false claims about the delivered code
evidence: SUMMARY.md:5 'implemented ... in TypeScript (Node.js)' and SUMMARY.md:22 'Stores data in SQLite (in-memory database)' / :39 'using in-memory for simplicity' — the code is JavaScript (server.js) and uses a file-backed DB (server.js:12 dbPath='./books.db'). FINAL_SUMMARY.md:63 claims 'Uses specified language (Node.js)' when stack.json specifies typescript.
suggestion: Delete the agent self-report files or correct them; a reader taking FINAL_SUMMARY.md at face value would wrongly conclude the language constraint was met.

title: Tests are not isolated — they share one persistent ./books.db behind a no-op beforeEach
evidence: test.js:9-12 beforeEach only calls done() with the comment 'we can just proceed with tests'; server.js:12 opens a fixed file DB './books.db' that is never truncated or deleted. Rows accumulate across every it() and across repeated `npm test` invocations.
suggestion: Point the DB at ':memory:' (or a per-worker temp file via an env var) and recreate the schema in beforeEach, so each test starts from a known state.

title: The ?author= filter test cannot fail if the filter is ignored
evidence: test.js:100-121 seeds only books by 'F. Scott Fitzgerald' and then asserts response.body.length > 0 and response.body[0].author === 'F. Scott Fitzgerald'. Every row in the shared DB has that author, so the assertions hold even if server.js:77-80 dropped the WHERE clause. R3 is verified by inspection of server.js, not by this test.
suggestion: Seed a second book by a different author and assert the filtered response excludes it (and that the unfiltered list includes it).

title: Prepared statements are created per request and never finalized; the DB handle is never closed
evidence: server.js:48 (POST), server.js:127 (PUT) and server.js:159 (DELETE) each call db.prepare(...) inside the handler; no .finalize() appears anywhere in server.js, and db.close() is never called. Each mutating request leaks a sqlite3 Statement.
suggestion: Use db.run(sql, params, cb) directly (it prepares and finalizes internally), or hoist the statements to module scope and finalize them on shutdown.

title: Route :id is passed to SQL unvalidated, so a malformed id returns 404 instead of 400
evidence: server.js:95, :117 and :157 take req.params.id verbatim; GET /books/abc binds 'abc' to the id column and yields no row, returning 404 'Book not found' (server.js:105-109) rather than a 400 for a non-numeric identifier.
suggestion: Parse the id with Number.parseInt and return 400 when it is not a positive integer.

title: Database path is a hard-coded relative './books.db' with no configuration hook
evidence: server.js:12 const dbPath = './books.db'; the value is never read from the environment, unlike the port at server.js:6 which honours process.env.PORT. server.js:3 requires 'path' but never uses it.
suggestion: Read the path from process.env.DB_PATH with './books.db' as the default, and drop the unused path import.
